rationale:
Evidence: iteration 1 (score 356.6) finished 18 of 20 oval trials at mean time 1.89 s, so base_speed 1.3 is fast enough. Both failures are off-track exits on the s-bend (progress 0.27) and slalom (progress 0.18), with max_error about 0.062 to 0.063 m against an off-track limit of about 0.0575 m. Iteration 0 showed the same near-0.06 m max_error at higher gain, so the limit is probably the sensor coverage on sharp bends rather than gain alone. The five sensors span only plus or minus 0.04 m. On a sharp bend the tape can slide outside that span, and the controller then has little signal before the line is lost.

Changes: (1) Widen the sensor span to plus or minus 0.06 m (x = -0.06, -0.03, 0, 0.03, 0.06), keeping the same weights, so the robot sees the line further out and keeps a signal through sharper bends. (2) Increase sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 m, the maximum, so each sensor keeps a nonzero reading at larger lateral error and line loss is less likely. (3) Raise kp from 2.5 to 3.0 for a firmer correction on the bends. (4) Raise kd from 0.8 to 1.0 to damp the larger correction. base_speed stays at 1.3, since the oval margin is comfortable. ki stays at 0.02 and the line_loss mode stays at last_direction.

Expected result: s-bend and slalom should stop ending off-track early, with progress well above 0.5 on the s-bend. Oval completion should hold, with a finish time under 2.5 s. Hypotheses: (a) the wider span is the main fix, so max_error on the s-bend and slalom should drop below 0.05 m; (b) line_loss_events should fall toward 0 on the s-bend; (c) if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3, kd is too low for the higher kp. Measurements to see next: per-track completion, progress, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation.
